git_scope: Blobless clone of the source's full history, and a checkout at the pinned commit for issue #715, the head of master when retrieved, made from that history's objects. The pin's parent is 5a299b4 (2026-10-20), whose parent d09edd7 (2026-10-19) is the child of 7b6c87e, the pin of issue #678; the three commits were pushed together at 2026-10-21T22:56:37Z, after the issue. The scope is the explicit certificate certificates/nN.cert and its credit record certificates/nN.json at each of the 173 counts at or below 1024 the issue claims, the four indexes the issue links (upper_bounds.json, certified_bounds.json, certificates/best/manifest.json, public_bounds.json), the provenance review and per-count provenance, the three READMEs, certificates/best/SHA256SUMS, the construction checker certificate_constructions.py, and the source's exact checker verify_bound_certificate.py with its MIT licence. The 139 certificates of the counts whose certificate was first committed after 7b6c87e are retained; the 34 certificates the issue restates from earlier public commits, and everything else in the scope, are pinned by digest only. The 1112 rows above 1024, the 857 witnesses under certificates/best/, certificates/parents/, certificates/extended/, the drawings, the search programs and the Rust and CUDA sources are pinned by the commit and were neither retained nor executed.
license: The repository states no licence for its data or prose: the tree has no LICENSE, and neither README.md nor the certificate READMEs state reuse terms. The 139 certificates are retained as factual data under the owner decision of 2026-10-09 recorded in resources/web/known-best-packings/README.md (Retained Factual Data). verify_bound_certificate.py states that it is Evan Daniel's MIT-licensed verifier with modifications by Francisco Couzo with Codex, under the MIT licence in BOUND_VERIFIER_LICENSE.txt (Copyright (c) 2026 Evan Daniel); both are byte-identical to the copies the couzo-issue678-2026-10-18 packet retains under that licence, and are pinned against them. Prose, indexes, manifests, credit records and the construction checker are hash-pinned and not copied.
claims: Issue #715 reports 1285 improved upper bounds for n = 328 to 9913, 173 at or below 1024 and 1112 above, each the exact side of the source's certificate or construction rounded up at 12 decimal places, with the exact certificate headers authoritative. At each of the 173 counts at or below 1024 the pin holds an explicit certificate certificates/nN.cert of n squares whose header side rounds up to the issue's print and equals the bound certified_bounds.json states; 29 of them are the index's L-border constructions and 9 its deletions, written out in full.

The issue says the rows include native and browser refinements and their square-tiling, repeated L-border and deletion consequences, not all independent discoveries; that both maintained exact geometry routes accept the finite source witnesses; and that the compared Goebel, strip, Friedman, tiling, L-border and deletion constructions do not match or beat any listed bound. Those runs and comparisons are the author's; no optimality claim is made.
